function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Paris is a fascinating city with so much to offer—whether you’re looking for iconic landmarks, cultural experiences, culinary delights, or just a quick snapshot of what makes it special. Below is a quick guide that covers the essentials, plus a few suggestions depending on your interests.

---

## Quick Snapshot

| Category | Highlights |
|----------|------------|
| **Capital** | France |
| **Population** | ~2.1 million (city proper) |
| **Language** | French |
| **Time Zone** | Central European Time (CET) / Central European Summer Time (CEST) |
| **Currency** | Euro (€) |
| **Best Time to Visit** | Spring (April–June) & Fall (September–October) – mild weather, fewer crowds |

---

## Must‑See Landmarks

| Landmark | Why It’s Worth It | Tips |
|----------|------------------|------|
| **Eiffel Tower** | Iconic symbol of Paris; panoramic city views | Book tickets online; visit at sunset for a magical light show |
| **Louvre Museum** | Home to the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and thousands of masterpieces | Arrive early; consider a guided audio tour |
| **Notre‑Dame Cathedral** | Gothic architecture (note: still under restoration after 2019 fire) | Explore the surrounding Île de la Cité; check for current visitor access |
| **Sacré‑Coeur & Montmartre** | Bohemian vibe, street artists, sweeping city views | Wander the cobblestone streets; visit the artists’ square (Place du Tertre) |
| **Champs‑Élysées & Arc de Triomphe** | Classic shopping & historic monument | Walk from Place de la Concorde to the Arc; climb to the top for a view of the Arc itself |
| **Palace of Versailles** | Opulent palace & gardens just outside Paris | Take a train (RER C) or a guided tour; book tickets in advance |

---

## Cultural Hotspots

| Activity | Where |
|----------|-------|
| **Museum of Modern Art (MOM)** | 11th arrondissement |
| **Centre Pompidou** | 4th arrondissement – modern art & architecture |
| **Musée d’Orsay** | 7th arrondissement – Impressionist masterpieces |
| **Opéra Garnier** | 9th arrondissement – stunning interior & tours |
| **Le Marais** | 3rd & 4th arrondissements – trendy boutiques, galleries, and historic sites |

---

## Food & Drink

| Dish | Where to Try |
|------|--------------|
| **Croissants & Pain au Chocolat** | Local boulangeries (e.g., Poilâne, Boulangerie Poilâne) |
| **Escargot** | Classic French restaurants (e.g., L’Arpège) |
| **Coq au Vin** | Traditional bistros (e.g., Le Relais de l’Entrecôte) |
| **Macarons** | Ladurée, Pierre Hermé |
| **Cheese & Wine** | Fromage shops (e.g., Fromagerie Quatrehomme) & wine bars (e.g., Le Baratin) |
| **Street Food** | Marché des Enfants Rouges, Rue Cler market |

---

## Practical Tips

| Topic | Advice |
|-------|--------|
| **Getting Around** | Metro & RER are fast; consider a multi‑day pass (Paris Visite). Biking via Vélib’ is also popular. |
| **Safety** | Pickpocketing can occur in tourist areas; keep valuables secure. |
| **Language** | Basic French phrases help; most locals speak English in tourist zones. |
| **Connectivity** | Free Wi‑Fi in many cafés; consider a local SIM or portable hotspot. |
| **Cash vs Card** | Cards are widely accepted; small shops may prefer cash. |

---

## Suggested Itineraries

### 1‑Day “Classic Paris”
- Morning: Eiffel Tower + Champ de Mars
- Mid‑day: Seine river cruise
- Afternoon: Louvre
- Evening: Dinner in the Latin Quarter

### 3‑Day “Culture & Cuisine”
- Day 1: Notre‑Dame, Sainte‑Chapelle, Île Saint-Louis
- Day 2: Montmartre, Sacré‑Coeur, Musée d’Orsay
- Day 3: Le Marais, Centre Pompidou, evening jazz club

### 5‑Day “Beyond the Basics”
- Days 1–3: Classic sights + day trip to Versailles
- Day 4: Day trip to Giverny (Monet’s Garden) or the Champagne region
- Day 5: Explore the Canal Saint‑Martin, trendy boutiques, and a farewell dinner

---

## Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Do I need a visa?** | EU/EEA citizens don’t. Non‑EU visitors may need a Schengen visa; check your country’s requirements. |
| **What’s the best way to buy museum tickets?** | Online pre‑booking saves time; many museums offer free entry on the first Sunday of each month. |
| **Is Paris safe for solo travelers?** | Generally yes; stay aware of pickpockets, especially in crowded areas. |
| **Can I use my phone for navigation?** | Yes—Google Maps, Citymapper, and the official Paris Metro app are reliable. |

---
